Professional Service Unit Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
| P a g e  4  
 
1. Introduction, Context and Principles 
1.1 Professional service unit review is a quality assurance and enhancement process 
that evaluates the quality, currency and strategic alignment of the provision of 
services by an individual professional service unit within the University. This 
includes:  
• the strategic direction of that unit;  
• 
its service strategy; and  
• its service activities.  
Professional service unit review is a core part of the University’s quality assurance 
infrastructure and is based on the internationally accepted review model outlined 
inter alia within the Standards and Guidelines for Quality Assurance in the European 
Higher Education Area (2015). Professional service unit review is conducted on a 
five-yearly cycle (or more frequently if required) and will normally be undertaken on 
a functional unit basis but may also consider smaller units within individual 
functions, as necessary2.  
 
1.2 This policy sets out the basis for the University’s conduct of professional service unit 
reviews. It is grounded in the following principles set out in the University Reviews 
Policy: 
• Alignment with the SETU Quality Framework document. 
• Awareness of emerging national and international developments, legislative 
or otherwise, regarding the provision of education and related services. 
• Regard for stakeholder expectations and requirements, as appropriate. 
• Commitment to continuous improvement as part of a cycle of periodic 
professional service unit review of the University’s service provision. 
 
1.3 A professional service unit should be understood as any area, department or 
function within the University which delivers a University service. This definition 
excludes academic units, which may be a faculty, a department or another sub-unit 
responsible for the development and delivery of programmes. It will be the 
responsibility of the relevant Vice President to determine the coherence of a 
professional service unit for the purpose of a professional service unit review.  
2. Purpose 
2.1 This policy details how the University intends to meet its requirements regarding 
internal quality review of its professional service units and their strategies, 
management and provision.  
 
2.2 This policy sets out the stages and outcomes of the professional service unit review 
process, and the responsibilities of the University, the relevant professional service 
 
2 Note: For clarity, ‘professional service unit’ will be used throughout this policy and accompanying procedure 
to refer to the unit undergoing professional service unit review.

Professional Service Unit Reviews Policy 
Version 1.0 
| P a g e  5  
 
unit and other relevant stakeholders involved in carrying out professional service 
unit review and responding to its outcomes. 
 
This policy further creates the basis for the University to develop a schedule of 
professional service unit reviews or to conduct reviews of specific services outside 
of that schedule where a need to do so is identified. In cases where a review of 
specific services is required, the review process will be guided by section 4 below, 
adapted as necessary. 
 
2.3 Finally, this policy seeks to ensure that appropriate action is taken following the 
conduct of professional service unit review and that review processes, their actions 
and consequent action taken by professional service units support a cycle of 
continuous improvement in the University’s service provision. 
3. Scope 
3.1 This policy applies to all of the University’s professional service units (excluding 
academic units, which are addressed under the Academic Unit Reviews Policy) and 
to other areas of the University identified in section 5 below. Staff are required to 
engage with the policy as necessary and are expected to participate in and 
contribute to reviews as appropriate. 
4. Policy 
4.1 Professional Service Unit Review  
Professional service unit review incorporates the review of all activity within a 
professional service unit. This includes the strategic direction of the professional 
service unit; its service strategy; its service activities and the monitoring, collection, 
analysis and review of data related to those activities and their delivery. 
Professional service unit review also includes the development of the services 
within the unit; the management of the services within the unit; the resourcing of 
the unit and the provision of services to and engagement with internal and external 
stakeholders (where relevant).  
This can (where appropriate) include services related to programmes leading to 
SETU awards that are provided through third-party arrangements with other 
providers of education and training, both nationally and internationally, as 
relevant.   
4.2 Review Objectives 
Professional service unit review provides a means for the University (and its 
individual professional service units) to:  
• 
assure the University of the currency, coherence, strategic alignment and 
quality of its service provision; service activity; service strategy; the 
management and delivery of its services; and to facilitate it to benchmark

| P a g e  6  
 
itself against that of peer educational institutions both in Ireland and 
internationally;  
• 
ensure that service delivery and activity within a professional service unit is 
reviewed and revised in line with contemporary best practice;  
• 
elicit and respond to feedback from University constituents and 
stakeholders and align its service delivery with the needs of stakeholders as 
relevant; 
• 
maintain public confidence in the University’s provision of services and 
services activity; 
• 
reflect upon the governance, management and operation of the University’s 
service delivery with a view to highlighting and disseminating good practice 
as well as identifying key opportunities, challenges and weaknesses, and 
implementing actions that will support development and improvement; 
• 
consider the effectiveness of quality assurance procedures for professional 
service unit review. 
 
4.3 Professional Service Unit Review Schedule 
Professional service unit reviews are scheduled and conducted in accordance with 
the University’s obligations and requirements. A schedule of professional service 
unit reviews is agreed by the University and reviews for each professional service 
unit are then arranged accordingly. 
 
4.4 Key Review Stages 
The key stages in each professional service unit review process are: 
Agreement of a timeline and terms of reference for the individual professional 
service unit review process between the relevant head(s) of the professional service 
unit (and, where they are not a member of the Executive Management Team, the 
key executive in the professional service unit) and the Office of the Vice President for 
Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning. Each review process will be in alignment 
with the overall professional service unit review schedule established by the Joint 
Quality Committee; 
a. Engagement by the professional service unit’s staff, as well as relevant internal 
and external stakeholders, in a self-evaluation process;  
b. Preparation of a self-evaluation report by the professional service unit through a 
self-evaluation committee; 
c. Review of the self-evaluation report (as part of a broader engagement process, 
typically including a site visit and meetings with relevant internal and external 
stakeholders) by an independent peer review group, who are appointed and 
approved by the Joint Quality Committee;

Version 1.0 
| P a g e  7  
 
d. Preparation of a peer review group report, to include recommendations of the 
peer review group; 
e. Consideration of the peer review group report by the professional service unit 
(including the unit’s executive lead) and drafting of the professional service unit’s 
response to the report through the executive lead; 
f. Development of a quality enhancement plan by the professional service unit 
arising from the report; 
g. Consideration of the outcome of the review process, including any 
recommendations, and approval of the quality enhancement plan by the 
University through Governing Body3 (through the Joint Quality Committee); 
h. Publication of the peer review group report on the University website to ensure 
transparency and dissemination of good practice and to promote public 
confidence; 
i. Ongoing monitoring by the University of the quality enhancement plan’s 
implementation by the professional service unit through submission of an annual 
update on implementation to the Joint Quality Committee. 
4.5 Review Guidelines 
Professional service units undergoing professional service unit review will be 
supported by guidelines for the conduct of review processes, which will be 
maintained by the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and 
Learning. 
4.6 Self-evaluation Process and Report 
A self-evaluation process based on the principles of constructive criticism, open and 
honest reflection on current practice and formulation of recommendations for 
improvement of provision, is central to the professional service unit review 
process.  
Responsibility to produce self-evaluation reports rests with professional service 
unit management. To support consistency of approach across the University, the 
Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning will 
develop and maintain a template for self-evaluation reports. 
4.7 Peer Review Group Composition 
The peer review group will include an appropriate balance of expertise and 
experience and will comprise a suitably qualified chair, an appropriate number of 
external representatives relevant to the professional service area (including 
representatives with relevant higher education experience), an external student 
representative, and a secretary, who is responsible for drafting the peer review 
group report, from the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching 
 
3 Where substantive matters of note need to be considered by Governing Body, these will be reported to 
Governing Body by the Joint Quality Committee.

| P a g e  8  
 
and Learning. Regard will be had to international representation and gender 
balance in the establishment of peer review groups. 
5. Responsibilities 
5.1 Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and Learning 
 
5.1.1 The organisation and operational management of professional service unit 
reviews is the responsibility of the Office of the Vice President for Academic 
Affairs, Teaching and Learning, in consultation with the management of the 
relevant professional service unit. 
 
5.1.2 Peer review group members will be provided with appropriate briefing and 
training by the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, Teaching and 
Learning to ensure their familiarity with the University’s context and that of the 
professional service unit under review. 
5.2 Joint Quality Committee 
The Joint Quality Committee is responsible for the formation of the professional 
service unit reviews policy, for approving the schedule of professional service unit 
reviews, for approving and appointing the composition of professional service unit 
peer review groups, for ensuring that professional service unit reviews are taking 
place and being reported on, and for ensuring that reviews are being completed 
and their outcomes implemented. The Committee is also responsible for making 
recommendations to Governing Body on relevant approvals. 
5.3 Executive Management Team 
The relevant Executive is responsible for considering the outcome of the review, 
drafting an executive response to the recommendations (which will focus on the 
financial impact of the quality enhancement plan), and submitting the quality 
enhancement plan for approval to Governing Body (through the Joint Quality 
Committee).  
5.4 Governing Body 
Governing Body (through the Joint Quality Committee) is responsible for the 
approval of the outcomes of professional service unit reviews – to include any 
recommendations, as well as the quality enhancement plan – and for ensuring the 
monitoring of the plan’s implementation by the professional service unit. 
5.5 Unit under Review 
The unit under review is responsible for undertaking a comprehensive self-
evaluation exercise of its activities, ensuring that all relevant stakeholders, internal 
and external to the unit, are involved in and/or consulted on the process. It will 
then record the process and its outcomes in a self-evaluation report. The unit 
under review is also responsible for ensuring that a representative selection of

internal and external stakeholders is available to meet with the peer review group 
during the site visit.  
Following the production of the review report, the unit under review will develop a 
quality enhancement plan, setting out how it intends responding to and 
implementing any recommendations proposed by the peer review group. As 
outlined above, the unit’s implementation of the quality enhancement plan will be 
monitored by the University.

7. Review of Policy 
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date, and/or as soon as possible 
following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
8. Author 
The author of this policy is the Office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs, 
Teaching and Learning. Any feedback or issues arising on implementation of this policy 
should be communicated to the policy author. The policy author is responsible for 
ensuring that the Policy Owner is aware of these comments when reviewing the policy. 
9. Compliance 
It is expected that all employees will comply with this policy.
